blocking: B1 (new bypass, same class as the earlier BLOCKING; reached through the real producer path). freshnessOf() at app.js L111-113 still shows a FRESH ('Before expiry') badge on expired LIVE data when expires_at is a form that Python accepts but JS Date.parse MISPARSES into a later instant. The earlier case was a form JS could not parse at all; this one parses, to the wrong time. Python 3.11 fromisoformat accepts any single character as the date/time separator. V8 treats '(' as the start of a comment and stops at U+0000, so it reads only the date part as midnight. Evidence: contract.parse_ts('2026-01-03(00:00+23:59') = 2026-01-02T00:01Z, but Date.parse gives 2026-01-03T00:00Z with TZ=UTC. The same holds for '2026-01-03\u000000:00+23:59'. Both pass through the fixture's own fx._assembled(fx._expiry(form)) path, i.e. producers.assembler.assemble_bundle at NOW=2026-01-02T00:00Z, which persists FRESH/FRESH. They also pass the unchanged web_mvp.validate_bundle (ACCEPT). Rendered in Chromium 1194 (Playwright 1.56.1), 'changes' shows FRESH at a browser clock of 2026-01-02T01:00Z, 59 minutes after the Python expiry, in UTC, Etc/GMT+12, Pacific/Kiritimati and Asia/Seoul. It also shows FRESH at 2026-01-02T12:00Z, 12 hours after expiry, in UTC, GMT+12 and Seoul (paren form) and in all four zones (NUL form). '2026-01-03(00:00:00+00:00' shows FRESH at 2026-01-03T06:00Z in Etc/GMT+12, 6 hours after its expiry. The window is bounded: about 24 hours for NUL, up to about 36 hours for '(' with an offset of +23:59 and a UTC-12 browser. At 2026-10-03 every form shows STALE. Fuzz evidence: 175,824 Python-accepted forms (dates × 100+ separators × times × offsets) plus 2,224,126 forms covering every Unicode code point as the separator.
